title: Founder case: HP's first product and first big customer

sources.claim: Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard began part-time work in a garage in Palo Alto with $538 in working capital; their first product was the HP 200A audio oscillator for testing sound equipment; Walt Disney Studios asked for changes and ordered eight of the modified model (200B) for the film Fantasia.

sections.skill: Apply a documented early decision: solve a specific need and adapt for a key customer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how much working capital did they start with?

choices.text: 538 dollars

questions.correct_answer: 538 dollars
questions.intro: Documented history (HP's own history pages): Bill Hewlett and Dave Packard began part-time work in a garage in Palo Alto, California, with 538 dollars in working capital. Their first product was the HP 200A audio oscillator, an instrument used to test sound equipment. Walt Disney Studios asked for changes and ordered eight of the modified model, the 200B, for the film Fantasia. Lesson drawn by this course (an interpretation): start with little capital, solve a specific problem for professional users, and adapt to a serious customer's request. One success story does not guarantee the same result for another business.
